text:
Cole Hutson has 15 points in 18 games as a 20-year-old on Washington's blue line, including the overtime winner in Ottawa on Nov. 10, and 11 points over his last ten. He is playing 19:30 a night and running a power-play unit that has produced five of those points.

Then he said this, in RMNB's headline: "I'm just not playing well enough." It is the right instinct, even if the scoresheet disagrees. His five goals come on 3.69 expected, and the Capitals have scored 4.6 more goals than expected with him on the ice, so the point pace has help. The five-on-five share is solid, 53.5% of expected goals, but about what the team does without him.

The comparison that matters: defensemen picked around 43rd overall scored a median 0.21 points a game in their first full season. He is at 0.83. In six tracked games this season, Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones has 33% of his setups going across the royal road, against 15% for a typical defenseman; small sample, big signature. A high-risk, high-reward style will have rough nights. Watch how Washington shelters him when the bounces even out.
headline: Hutson is ahead of the curve, and hard on himself
